Integers and Rectangles: Winkler's Proof

InvariantsGraph TheoryLogic
Game: Find a path across a tiled rectangle that proves one of its sides is a whole number.
How to play: Pick a tiling, toggle the decoration and borders, and click a tile to swap its colour.

Look for the math

Peter Winkler's proof turns a tiling puzzle into a path puzzle very like the game of Hex.

Colour and decorate

Green tiles have an integer width; red tiles have an integer height. Give each tile thin strips of the opposite colour along its integer-length sides: green tiles get red strips above and below, red tiles get green strips left and right. Now a green region can only be crossed sideways and a red region only vertically. Just as in Hex, one of two things must happen: a green path joins the left and right edges, or a red path joins the top and bottom.

Reading off the answer

A green path passes through whole green widths, which add to the big width; a red path adds whole red heights to the big height. Either way the big rectangle has an integer side. The logic test checks which path occurs in three tilings and confirms that the widths or heights along the path sum exactly to the corresponding side.

Uncheck "Decorate" and check "Show borders". Does the path you see still prove the theorem?

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)
